items.headline: Senate Finance Text 'Expected Today' Per Punchbowl — Legislative Tracking Confirms June 6; June 1 Target Structurally at Risk; Hoyle WAR Act Blocks Iran War Reconciliation Funding
items.summary: Two domestic-economic developments. First: Punchbowl News characterizes May 17 as a 'critical phase' for reconciliation with Finance text 'expected out today,' but per legislative tracking this expectation will not be met — the Finance Committee text is confirmed to arrive June 6, a full 22 days past the May 15 deadline and 5 days past Trump's June 1 target. The 'expected today' Punchbowl framing reflects ongoing optimism within the Finance Committee's own communications but continues the slip pattern established by the May 15 miss: Finance's publicly communicated 'expected' dates are running 3+ weeks ahead of actual text release. The DHS/Judiciary $72 billion package cleared for floor remains waiting on Finance as the binding downstream constraint. June 1 reconciliation target is structurally at risk. Second: Rep. Val Hoyle (D-OR) introduced the No War Appropriations through Reconciliation (WAR) Act, which would prohibit any reconciliation bill from appropriating budget authority for hostilities against Iran unless Congress has authorized those hostilities through a formal declaration of war or AUMF. The legislation is unlikely to pass with Republican Senate control, but its introduction is significant for three reasons: it raises the procedural and constitutional question of whether Iran war funding through reconciliation is permissible under existing statute; it provides a clean Democratic policy marker against any reconciliation provision funding post-Project Freedom operations; and it reinforces Sen. Rand Paul's already-stated opposition to Iran war funding through reconciliation — a Republican defection that, if sustained, tightens the margin for a reconciliation majority even before the Finance text is released.
